subject: Trial realignment request — burn rate mismatch and credit swap proposal
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantime.io>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Quantime Billing <billing@quantime.io>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial cadence and burn concerns — need flexibility

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for getting our evaluation started last month — the team is up and running and we appreciate the quick onboarding. After monitoring usage the last two weeks we have a mismatch between how we expected traffic to ramp and how our device fleet actually hit the models. Our burn is front-loaded (~65% in week 1) and we're worried the scheduled end date will arrive before we can validate latency at scale.

Two asks:
- Is there a way to shift the remaining days of the timeboxed trial to later in October (i.e., pause & resume) rather than losing them?
- Alternatively, could Redwood convert unused days into a small pool of inference credits we can draw down? Our finance team would prefer credits tied to usage instead of a straight extension.

I've attached a short burn report so you can see the pattern. We're flexible on how this is accomplished — engineers care most about steady windows for load tests, finance cares about predictable accounting.

Appreciate any options you can offer by EOD Monday so we can let internal stakeholders know.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, Quantime

Attachment: quantime_burn_report_Q3.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantime.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial cadence and burn concerns — need flexibility

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the note and the burn report — helpful. Short answer: yes, we can avoid forcing a hard cut-off that would lose the remaining evaluation capacity. I sketched two operational paths for you and finance:

Option A — Pause & resume timebox (engineering-preferred)
- We put the trial in a paused state for up to 21 days. Remaining evaluation days are preserved and will resume when you flip the flag.
- Engineering: steady window for burst tests.
- No additional charge, but we require a written confirmation of the pause window to keep things auditable.

Option B — Convert remaining days to usage credits (finance-preferred)
- Convert the N remaining days into an equivalent token/compute-credit bucket (valid for 60 days).
- Credits are applied to hosted inference consumption and shown on invoices as a negative line item; usable across any model you run in the account.
- We can also offer a small 10% bonus on converted credits (e.g., convert $10k of days -> $11k credit) as a one-time concession if you commit to a short follow-on PO within 90 days.

If you want, Ben can provide the exact conversion math (how we map your remaining allocated days -> token/credit value, and the invoice flow). Marissa can scope the pause window and audit trail we need for your compliance team.

Which approach should we draft for the billing/procurement story? Happy to draft the credit proposal and send a signed confirmation template for the pause if you pick A.

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Lukas Meyer
Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0184

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantime.io>, lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Credit conversion math and invoice treatment (proposal attached)

Hi Elena — looping in the conversion details as requested. I ran the numbers against the burn report you sent and two scenarios look straightforward:

Scenario 1 — Straight conversion (conservative)
- Remaining 9 evaluation days -> equivalent of 18,000 token-credits at your current trial profile.
- Credit validity: 60 days from issuance.
- Invoice: line item "Trial Credit Adjustment (Quantime)" applied to next invoice; accounting will see a negative credit balance.

Scenario 2 — Conversion + incentive (recommended)
- Same conversion but we add a 10% bonus credit (i.e., 19,800 token-credits).
- Requires a short-form PO for a follow-on pilot at a committed minimum spend of $30k within 90 days (no model lock-in).

Attached: lukas_credit_proposal_v2.pdf — includes the exact token math, example invoices, and a one-page confirmation template for the pause (if you choose Option A instead).

If you prefer option A, we can prepare the pause confirmation now and mark your trial as paused the day we receive signed confirmation.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers if that helps procurement.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: lukas_credit_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf, 62KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantime.io>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Quantime Billing <billing@quantime.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial cadence and burn concerns — need flexibility

Thanks Lukas and Ben — this is great and gives finance and engineering something concrete to agree on. Quick answers from our side:

- Engineering prefers Option A (pause & resume) so we can preserve a contiguous window for load testing.
- Finance would accept Option B if you include the 10% conversion bonus and we don't have to open an RFP; however, procurement asked if the credits can have 90-day validity instead of 60 to allow for scheduling.

Proposal: Let's do Option A with a 21-day pause now. If by the end of the pause we haven't used the days, Quantime requests the conversion to credits with the 10% bonus and 90-day validity (i.e., a fallback). Please prepare the pause confirmation and the short PO template for the potential credit conversion.

If you can send both documents by EOD Friday I'll get them routed internally. Also looping in our billing contact for the paperwork.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Elena

Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, Quantime
